summary: electro-session harvests browser passwords, cookies, and keychain material and uploads them to remote blob storage
details: electro-session@0.1.0 presents itself as 'Session utilities' with a blank README ('Private package'), but its exported API surface (dist/index.d.ts) is that of a browser credential stealer. SessionData exposes passwords, cookies, passwordsPath, cookiesPath, keychainOk (OS-keychain decryption status), encryptionKeyPath, blobUrls, and gcsUrls. SessionsOptions exposes blobToken, blobPrefix, blobAccess ('private'|'public'), uploadKey, and cleanupLocal. The package depends on @vercel/blob at runtime and ships two heavily obfuscated entrypoints, dist/cli.js and a ~1MB dist/index.js, both processed with javascript-obfuscator (listed in devDependencies) using a rotated string array plus an RC4-over-base64 decoder that reconstructs identifiers, URLs, filesystem paths, and API endpoints at runtime. The cleanupLocal + uploadKey + blob-upload combination is the shape of a stealer that removes on-disk evidence of the harvested credentials after transmission to a remote object-storage destination whose token/URLs are embedded inside the obfuscated bundle rather than supplied by the caller.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
